results.title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu’s party for ‘marathon’ Israeli coalition talks
results.content: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has invited caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party for coalition talks, his centrist Yashar party said Saturday. The "marathon series of talks" starts Sunday, the party said, adding that the move reflected a commitment to form "the broadest possible government" after the October election failed to deliver an outright winner.

results.title: France’s sixth consecutive Saturday of protests draw lower turnout
results.content: Turnout ⁠was down ​at largely peaceful demonstrations across France on the sixth consecutive Saturday of protests ​over the cost of living, with the interior ministry putting the figure at 82,500 across the country. Organisers said 150,000 people participated in the nationwide protests, down from their 200,000 figure last week.

results.title: 'Worst Ever' COP Summit?
results.content: Is this the worst COP summit on record? With limited political leadership, no official US delegation and mounting frustration over bureaucratic delays, questions are being raised about the effectiveness of the climate negotiations. Juan Carlos Beldsoe, a former White House climate adviser under Bill Clinton, described the process as labyrinthine and ultimately dispiriting. France 24's Gavin Lee speaks with climate advocate and six-time COP delegate, Henna Hundal about what this means for the future of global climate action.

results.title: Russia attacks Zelensky's hometown, Ukraine reaffirms wish to join NATO
results.content: A Russian ballistic missile attack on President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday killed two people and wounded dozens. Hours later, Zelensky reiterated his country's determination to join NATO, following proposals to provide Kyiv with security guarantees similar to those of the military alliance.

results.title: Russia launches ballistic missile attack on Zelensky's hometown in central Ukraine
results.content: A Russian ballistic missile attack on President Volodymyr Zelensky’s hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday killed two people and wounded dozens. Hours later, Zelensky reiterated his country's determination to join NATO. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kyiv.

results.title: Drone attack sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in Gulf of Finland
results.content: A Russian cargo ship caught fire after ​being hit by drones in the Baltic Sea on Saturday and drifted into Finnish waters. Reporting from Kyiv, FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg notes that the ship is affiliated with a major Russian military logistics company. While Ukrainian authorities typically neither confirm nor deny responsibility, analysts cite a clear motive for the targeting, Cragg explains.

results.title: COP31: Deep divisions persist over energy, finance and science
results.content: COP31 climate talks in Turkey have gone into overtime, with deep divisions over fossil fuels, climate finance and global warming targets delaying an agreement. A revised draft dropped all mention of fossil fuels, prompting strong criticism from the EU and a dozen countries demanding a clear commitment to phase them out. Negotiators are also split over a proposed global electrification target, carbon capture and the future of UN climate science reports. Developing nations have voiced anger over the removal of a $120 billion climate adaptation funding target. Australia is now racing to secure a revised deal before delegates leave. France 24 journalist Adria Rocha Cutiller tells us the latest.

results.title: FBI criminal database hacked
results.content: The FBI is investigating a reported major cyberattack targeting its national law enforcement database, the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which holds sensitive criminal justice records, including information on fugitives, missing persons, criminal histories and stolen property. President Donald Trump said he had just been briefed on the incident, describing it as “not good”. FRANCE 24’s Fraser Jackson reports from Washington DC.

results.title: Man convicted of starting palisades fire
results.content: A Los Angeles County jury found former rideshare driver Jonathan Rinderknecht guilty on Friday of starting the 2025 Palisades fire, which caused widespread destruction and loss of life. He faces a prison sentence of between five and 40 years. Liza Kaminov has more.

results.title: French police officers convicted of racist assault
results.content: A French court on Friday sentenced three policemen to serve time over the beating of a black music producer in 2020. It also recognized the assault on Michelle Zecler was racially motivated.

results.title: Endurance athlete swims in Hormuz Strait
results.content: The Strait of Hormuz remains largely blocked, with Iran attacking vessels attempting to cross it. As concerns grow over the environmental impact of the war, with toxic chemicals spreading through the air and sea, one swimmer and ocean advocate has gone a step further than issuing warnings: he plunged into the polluted and dangerous waters of the strait, calling on all sides to end the conflict.

results.title: France: Demonstrations losing steam as movement enters sixth week
results.content: Around 2,200 people took part in protests across France by 2pm local time, according to the Interior Ministry, which recorded 44 demonstrations nationwide and seven arrests, with the situation described as generally calm. Turnout was lower than on previous Saturdays. Reporting from Place de la République in Paris, FRANCE 24’s Antonia Kerrigan said rent rights organisations had also joined the sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, highlighting their growing pan-European dimension, with demonstrations taking place in seven European countries, including Spain, Portugal, Greece and Germany, where rising living costs and access to affordable housing are among the main concerns.

results.title: Countries race to secure Cop31 deal
results.content: COP31 climate talks have overrun their schedule as countries race to agree on a new global climate deal, following criticism of an earlier draft that made no mention of fossil fuels. The EU has warned that the current proposal risks turning the summit into a “fossil fuel summit”, as negotiators work towards a revised, potentially final agreement expected later today. France 24 International affairs editor Jamie Smith-Maillet tells us more.

results.title: New day of protests across France
results.content: France faces a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, with demonstrators taking to the streets to rally over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election. France 24 journalist Antonia Kerrigan tells us more.

results.title: Mexico captures drug cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ after deadly firefight
results.content: Mexico's military forces captured ​one of the most wanted suspected drug lords, Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro," the military announced on Saturday, after a deadly firefight that killed seven suspected attackers and four soldiers. Flores, one of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives, was flown to Mexico City after his capture.

results.title: Cargo ship runs aground off French coast
results.content: A Maltese-flagged cargo ship remains stranded off the coast of south-western France after running aground. French authorities are preparing an operation to prevent the vessel from capsizing and potentially causing pollution. The ship was not carrying any cargo, and all 19 crew members were safely evacuated by helicopter. Dan Quinlan reports.

results.title: Russia tests NATO’s eastern defences
results.content: Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland on Friday in what Prime Minister Donald Tusk said was likely an "intentional provocation" timed to coincide with European military exercises in the country for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine. Senior Lecturer in Conflict and Security at King's College in London, Domitilla Sagramoso, shares further insights.

results.title: Thousands protest overs prices, education, military spending in France and Europe
results.content: France is bracing for a sixth consecutive Saturday of protests, with demonstrators expected to rally over the rising cost of living and the government's handling of weeks of social unrest ahead of next year's presidential election. France 24 journalist Antonia Kerrigan tells us the latest from Paris.

results.title: Drone attack sets Russian cargo ship ablaze in Gulf of Finland
results.content: A Russian cargo ship caught fire after a drone strike in international waters in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday and later drifted into Finnish ⁠territorial waters, Finnish authorities said. Helsinki alerted NATO and imposed temporary restrictions in the area amid heightened tensions in the Baltic Sea.

results.title: Ethiopia: Tackling period poverty and stigma
results.content: In Ethiopia, entrepreneur Hanan Ahmed is tackling period poverty and the stigma surrounding menstruation. By producing affordable reusable sanitary pads and raising awareness in schools, she hopes to make menstrual health more accessible and help girls stay in class. Report by Awa Diouf & Guillaume Gougeon.

results.title: Ethiopia - Eritrea: Troops mobilise along the border
results.content: More than 200 former Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) fighters surrendered to Ethiopia’s federal military Friday, state-affiliated media reported, amid escalating border tensions with neighboring Eritrea. France 24 correspondent Tom Canetti tells us the latest.

results.title: Music strikes a chord at French protest
results.content: Throughout history, protest songs have brought people together across genres, rallying against war, racism, inequality and the establishment. Music is also playing a key role in the youth-led demonstrations here in France. Our reporters went to meet some of the musicians using their voices to express the protesters’ demands.

results.title: 'Accept cookies'? Russia collects data from swaths of unknowing Swedes
results.content: A Russian tech firm backed by an oligarch close to President Vladimir Putin has secretly been collecting data from hundreds of thousands – possibly millions – of Swedes, a newspaper investigation found. The revelation has rattled the Nordic nation, whose proximity to Russia and unusually open public records system make it particularly vulnerable to Moscow’s hybrid war tactics.

results.title: 'Unacceptable': EU chief condemns alleged Russian plot to kill US-Ukrainian citizen
results.content: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned an alleged Russian intelligence plot to assassinate a US-Ukrainian citizen in Denmark, vowing full solidarity with Copenhagen.
